counterfactual_missing_items: No thrombocytopenia or schistocytes/MAHA to support TTP
No endomyocardial biopsy or cardiac MRI confirming myocarditis
No viral PCR or serology result linking the febrile prodrome
decisive_items: Moderately depressed biventricular function (ejection fraction 42%; normal range >55%)
response.rationale: R2 uniquely pairs acute myocardial injury with objective biventricular failure, directly explaining shock and cardiac dysfunction. R4 cites ADAMTS13/vWF changes but lacks the obligatory thrombocytopenia and MAHA of TTP, and these labs can be secondary in critical illness. R5 is a downstream cardiogenic-shock phenotype without the troponin evidence; R1/C1 ARDS is confounded by depressed LV function; R3 has no raw support; R6 is nonspecific organ injury with normal fibrinogen against DIC.

rejected.why: No raw support spans supplied; septic shock is only a non-raw interpretation of shock and vasopressor use.
Bilateral opacities and oxygenation index meet ARDS but do not explain troponin elevation or biventricular failure and are confounded by cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
Kidney and liver injury with coagulopathy are nonspecific, and normal fibrinogen argues against DIC.
Depressed biventricular function and tricuspid regurgitation are also present in myocarditis; it lacks the troponin/ST evidence and represents a complication rather than the primary diagnosis.
Append-only completion of R1 with no additional raw evidence and the same ARDS limitation.
